overview.overviewText: This chapter explores Basic Concepts of Rotational Motion, Torque, Angular Momentum and Conservation, providing comprehensive conceptual analysis, mathematical relationships, and structured applications grounded in NCERT authority.

blocks.title: 1. Key Academic Principles: Basic Concepts of Rotational Motion, Torque, Angular Momentum and Conservation
blocks.contentMarkdown: The vector product of two vectors A and B is C = A x B = |A| * |B| * sin(theta) * n_hat and is anti-commutative: A x B = - (B x A). Torque tau of a force F acting at position vector r with respect to an origin is defined as tau = r x F. Angular momentum L of a particle with position vector r and linear momentum p is defined as L = r x p.

blocks.title: 2. Key Academic Principles: Basic Concepts of Rotational Motion, Torque, Angular Momentum and Conservation
blocks.contentMarkdown: The time rate of change of angular momentum of a particle or system equals the applied net external torque: dL/dt = tau_ext. The Law of Conservation of Angular Momentum states that if total external torque is zero, total angular momentum remains constant. The magnitude of torque is |tau| = r * F * sin(theta) = F * r_perp, with SI unit newton-metre (N*m).

blocks.title: 3. Key Academic Principles: Basic Concepts of Rotational Motion, Torque, Angular Momentum and Conservation
blocks.contentMarkdown: Magnitude: |tau| = r * F * sin(theta) = F * r_perp, where r_perp is the perpendicular distance from the axis/origin to the line of action of force (lever arm).
